bug_semantics: A malicious repository can put traversal components in a .gitmodules section name. GitPython parses that attacker-controlled section name without validation, assigns it to Submodule._name, and during Submodule.update(init=True) uses it to form <parent git dir>/modules/<name>. The resulting escaped path is passed to directory and clone operations, so initialization creates an attacker-controlled Git repository outside the intended clone directory.
flaw_origin: Commit 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc introduced _module_abspath() with os.path.join(parent_repo.git_dir, 'modules', name) and changed the initialization branch of Submodule.update() from the tree-backed submodule path to this unchecked name-derived path before Repo.clone_from(). That is the first causal connection between an untrusted .gitmodules name and the filesystem repository-creation sink; the pre-existing unchecked sm_name() parser alone did not create this attack path.
ai_marker: absent — git cat-file -p 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc shows author Sebastian Thiel <byronimo@gmail.com>, committer Sebastian Thiel <byronimo@gmail.com>, and a plain message with no Co-Authored-By, Assisted-by, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer/marker
evidence: The first-party advisory https://github.com/gitpython-developers/GitPython/security/advisories/GHSA-hmq2-w58f-27jc states that <=3.1.57 is affected and >=3.1.58 is patched. It identifies the flow sm_name(section) -> Submodule.iter_items() assigning sm._name -> _module_abspath() joining parent_repo.git_dir/modules/name -> clone/filesystem operations, and documents a released-3.1.57 PoC that creates /tmp/gitpython_poc_escaped_root/modules_dir while core Git rejects the suspicious name.

At 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc, git/objects/submodule/util.py sm_name() returns section[11:-1] unchecked; git/objects/submodule/base.py iter_items() reads n = sm_name(sms) and assigns sm._name = n. The same commit adds _module_abspath() at then-lines 204-210, whose Git-file branch returns os.path.join(parent_repo.git_dir, 'modules', name).

The 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc diff changes the Submodule.update() initialization branch from module_path = join_path_native(self.repo.working_tree_dir, self.path) to module_path = self._module_abspath(self.repo, self.path, self.name), after which Repo.clone_from(self.url, module_path, n=True) creates the repository. The path value in the parent was constrained by the required pc.tree[path] lookup; the newly used section name was not validated.

Immediate-parent tree verification: git rev-parse 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc^ returns a9a5414300a245b6e93ea4f39fbca792c3ec753f. git grep on that exact parent tree finds neither _module_abspath nor a git_dir/modules/name join. Direct inspection of the parent update branch shows only join_path_native(self.repo.working_tree_dir, self.path) feeding Repo.clone_from(). The BIC tree contains _module_abspath at base.py:204, the unchecked join at :206, and update's call at :422.

git log -L over _module_abspath traces the function through formatting/type-only edits to its zero-line addition in 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc. The next commit 67680a0877f01177dc827beb49c83a9174cdb736 extracts the same behavior into _clone_repo() and is therefore a refactor, not the BIC; the vulnerable update-to-clone path already exists in 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc.

Release boundary: git for-each-ref --contains identifies 0.3.6 as the earliest release tag containing the BIC. Peeled tag commits are 0.3.5=a2d39529eea4d0ecfcd65a2d245284174cd2e0aa (does not contain the BIC) and 0.3.6=4df4159413a4bf30a891f21cd69202e8746c8fea (does contain it). Thus this exact name-based mechanism first shipped in 0.3.6 and persisted through the advisory's last vulnerable release 3.1.57.

The direct patch e4b8e7d026ca6abb4cf604f8e77093432ce23c06 (commit subject 'Validate submodule names before filesystem operations', message naming GHSA-hmq2-w58f-27jc) adds _validated_name(), rejecting empty, absolute/drive-qualified, and '..'-component names before the modules/name join and other filesystem mutations. It landed on the mainline through merge commit 2212c6396dac0b2a8f03fc2e6708c72b6f363cc9 (PR #2202).

Follow-up direct commit 4299c990e1ca21896f9485277caf7bb0ae5b404c moves validation before the Git-version path branch and landed via f67029c3a28de20f12e537b87a1a1ff801c521d7. Both merges and both direct commits are ancestors of peeled tag 3.1.58=30be45d786e95023e23c616fec5cbabca861b44c; e4b8e7d026ca6abb4cf604f8e77093432ce23c06 is not an ancestor of peeled tag 3.1.57=ccbd573ac4ab52ccdcf395c400e600d5809bcc88. The 3.1.58 changelog explicitly lists GHSA-hmq2-w58f-27jc.

BIC-only AI attribution: the raw 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc commit object has a human author and committer and no trailers or AI markers. AI markers present on the 2026 fix commits are fix-only evidence and are excluded from BIC attribution under the protocol.
reasoning: The vulnerability begins with attacker control of the .gitmodules section name, but that parser behavior is not by itself the filesystem flaw. The smallest real BIC is 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc because it first derives the submodule repository location from that unchecked name and routes update initialization's clone to the result. Its immediate parent instead clones to the submodule path, which must correspond to a tree entry, and contains no name-derived modules path. Later commit 67680a0877f01177dc827beb49c83a9174cdb736 merely factors the already-vulnerable behavior into _clone_repo(). Tag ancestry places the mechanism after 0.3.5, beginning in 0.3.6, through 3.1.57. Direct patch e4b8e7d026ca6abb4cf604f8e77093432ce23c06 adds name validation, merge 2212c6396dac0b2a8f03fc2e6708c72b6f363cc9 lands it, and the validation-order follow-up is also present in 3.1.58. Because the BIC commit object contains no AI authorship/co-authorship marker and is authored and committed by Sebastian Thiel, the closed verdict is NOT_AI regardless of AI assistance disclosed only on the later fix.
